name: Laurel Ridge Community College

degree_context.general_education_authority: Laurel Ridge Computer Science Degree Curriculum Requirements

residency.rule: At least 25 percent of the credits required for the degree must be earned at Laurel Ridge Community College.

modeling_notes: The catalog publishes a categorical Computer Science Degree Curriculum Requirements list followed by Suggested Scheduling. Only the categorical list is composed.
The eight-credit natural-science requirement is the fixed CHM 111 and CHM 112 sequence, not a generic science category.

The elective requirement is two distinct courses totaling 5-8 credits from the exact printed pool. A course used in the separate Computer Systems and Digital Design requirement cannot reuse the same applied credits as an elective.

The fixed requirements total 55 credits, so the printed 5-8 elective range models 60-63 credits even though the page publishes a 60-64 program total. The unresolved one-credit maximum discrepancy remains explicit.

data_quality_flags.message: The fixed 55 credits plus the printed 5-8 elective range yield 60-63 credits, while Program Total is printed as 60-64.
Exactly two electives must total 5-8 credits; CSC 295 and CSC 298 each carry variable 1-5 credits.

narrative: Students will demonstrate their information literacy skills by effectively locating, evaluating, and utilizing various digital development resources.
Students will investigate factors other than computational efficiency that influence the choice of algorithms.
Students will compare different methods for converting numerical data from one format to another.
Students will illustrate the concepts of modeling and abstraction with respect to problem-solving.
Students will compare practical examples to the appropriate set, function, or relation model and interpret the associated operations and terminology in context.
Students will use at least one national or international user interface design standard in a simple application.
Students will explain the characteristics that distinguish the database approach from the approach of programming with data files.
